gaps.addiction: Not thin for treatment: the Weber-Morgan Health Department list (January 2025) is current and names the core Ogden providers, and its phones mostly matched the providers' own pages. Thin elsewhere: 211's Weber-Morgan list gives names and phones only; Intermountain's handout is broad but half Salt Lake and Davis County, phone-only, with several numbers that disagree with the providers' own pages (BAART, Weber Recovery Center); the WSU referral book is stale (old addresses for Weber Human Services and Clinical Consultants). Support groups (AA, NA, the Church's Addiction Recovery Program), sober living and harm reduction appear with conflicting or unverified phones and would need Scout's own search. Ogden's 211 search pages could not be read (search.211utah.org did not resolve).
gaps.children-pregnancy: Pregnancy and young-child help in Ogden is well covered by current official lists: the Weber-Morgan Health Department's April 2026 referral flyer and the State maternal resource guide (2025-26) name most front doors with phones. Thin spots: almost nothing for children's clothing, diapers or baby gear beyond Catholic Community Services and Welcome Baby's occasional supplies; no listed low-cost childcare beyond YCC and Head Start; nothing for older children and teens except afterschool clubs and JJYS youth centres whose walk-in access is unclear. The 211 lists are names and phones only and partly wrong (a pregnancy-center entry carries the old Pregnancy Riskline number; Children's Service Society shares DCFS's number; Youth Impact, Nurse-Family Partnership, MotherToBaby and Early Intervention each have conflicting phones across lists). The Ogden City guide (2022) has only a few child entries. 211's live search (search.utah211.org) did not resolve.
gaps.clothing-household: Thin. No Ogden or Weber County official source has a clothing or furniture list. The two 211 PDFs give names and phones only, and their 'Household Items / Furniture / Clothing' section is half thrift stores and half shelters or programmes that mention clothing in passing. The 211 online database is the best source, but several of its clothing records are Archived or Temporary Non-Operational (Salvation Army vouchers and thrift store, DI and DWS vouchers). No free furniture bank, baby-gear closet or school clothing closet for Ogden showed up on any readable list. St. Vincent de Paul and the Genesis Serve Center appear only via an aggregator that blocks reading or conflicting 211 data. Free clothing in Ogden comes down to two programmes, the Salvation Army closet (twice a month) and the Rescue Mission (twice a week). Scout would need its own search here, especially for furniture.
gaps.disability: Ogden has no official disability list. The 211 Weber-Morgan sheet's disability section is six phone numbers (VR, DSPD, EnableUtah, RISE, Roads to Independence, Special Needs Registry) with no addresses, and one Roads to Independence number it prints differs from the provider's own; the Ogden City guide names only EnableUtah and is from 2022. The health department sheet has no disability heading at all. The only rich list is the Utah Parent Center's Weber/Davis guide, which is for parents of children and mixes in Davis-only and Salt Lake providers, private clinics, private tutors and national websites. Nothing found lists adult disability supports beyond employment: no personal-care, respite, accessible-housing or benefits-application help (e.g. SSI/SSDI application assistance) specific to Ogden. Phone numbers conflicted across lists for Early Intervention, both school districts, DSPD and the Special Needs Registry, so Scout's own search and a phone check would still be needed.
gaps.domestic-violence: Thin but consistent. Every list agrees Ogden has one domestic-violence provider, YCC Family Crisis Center, plus the state LINKline and the national hotline; beyond those three the lists fill out with crime-victim, legal, sexual-assault and homeless-shelter entries that fail rule 2. The official lists (Weber County Attorney) are undated and give phones without addresses, and one still uses St. Anne's Center for Lantern House; 211's 2024-2025 Weber-Morgan sheet is current but names only, and labels the national hotline as the 'Domestic Violence Information Line'; the Weber State referral book is stale; the Weber-Morgan DV Coalition's resource page returns 404. Not found on any list: a DV-specific legal clinic, a victim-side counselling programme other than YCC's, or anything in Spanish. The open questions (prosecutor and police victim advocates, protective-order clerk, ISAT) are whether they belong here or under legal.
gaps.education: Ogden has no list devoted to education. The best sources are the state's adult-education directory (current, but adult education only) and the Weber-Morgan Health Department's May 2025 sheet; the Ogden City guide has the broadest education section but is dated February 2022 and leans on Weber State sub-programmes and summer children's activities. Both 211 lists fold education into an employment column, so most of their entries are job agencies, and 211's own search site does not resolve. There is no adult literacy (reading) tutoring programme, no citizenship-class provider confirmed, and no tutoring for school-age children on any list. Ogden School District's websites block automated reading, so its adult education and district phone numbers could not be confirmed and conflict between lists.
gaps.employment: Employment lists for Ogden exist but are short and repeat the same handful of names (DWS, Cottages of Hope, OWCAP, the Church employment centre, Job Corps, Futures Through Training), padded with schools and colleges. Only the Weber-Morgan Health flyer (April 2026) gives addresses; the 211 list gives phone numbers only, and 211's online search cannot be read without JavaScript. Phone numbers disagree between lists for DWS (four different numbers) and addresses disagree between 211 entries for the Church centre. Missing from every list: second-chance or re-entry employment help, day-labour and work-today options, and the DWS refugee and veterans employment programmes; Vocational Rehabilitation appeared only under Disabilities. Job Corps' status after the 2025 national pause needs a phone check.
gaps.financial-assistance: Thin. No Ogden or Weber County list has a Financial Assistance heading: the current 211 Weber-Morgan sheet lumps money help into Housing/Utilities and Employment with phone numbers only, Ogden City's guide is from 2019, and the court district's list (2023) has a single credit-counselling entry in Midvale. The direct emergency-cash front doors the lists and aggregators point to are mostly gone or paused: Catholic Community Services' Ogden site now describes food only, Cottages of Hope's bill help is paused for funding, Weber Housing Authority's rent payment line is marked non-operational on 211, and the Salvation Army's phone-based rent/utility help covers only unnamed zip codes. What reliably remains is HEAT (utility bills), OWCAP (call to see what is funded), DWS cash assistance and Cottages of Hope coaching. Scout would have to do the work to find any current one-time emergency rent/utility grant in Ogden (churches, St. Vincent de Paul conferences, United Way of Northern Utah), and to read 211's live search, which was not readable here beyond single service pages.
gaps.food: No official Ogden City, Weber County or Weber Human Services food list was found, and the Utah Food Bank pantry finder is a map that cannot be read. The only human-maintained list is 211's Weber-Morgan sheet (September 2024), which gives phone numbers only. Everything else came from aggregators that disagree on church pantries' phones, addresses and days; four church pantries (Griffin Memorial, Seventh-day Adventist, Hope Resurrected, First Baptist Ogden) have no page of their own, so they stay unclear until someone calls them. The school-district pantries (Weber and Ogden) had no readable page with hours. 211's own provider pages (utahdhhs.211utah.org/provider/...) are readable and were used to check, but its search could not be used as a list.
gaps.homeless-services: Ogden has few homeless providers and the lists agree on the same four shelters (Lantern House, Ogden Rescue Mission, Family Promise, Youth Futures), so overlap is high and coverage looks complete for shelter. Missing everywhere: a named coordinated-entry front door for Weber County (the Local Homeless Council page names none; the state's mydoorway.utah.gov/homelessness page is dead, returning 'Site not found'), any day center separate from the shelters, and hours. The 211 search pages do not render without JavaScript, Lantern House's own site shows no contact details, and Family Promise's site hides its address, so contact details came from the health-department sheet and 211 provider pages. The Church ICP and aggregator lists are mostly Salt Lake.
gaps.housing: Thin. No list names more than about six Ogden housing providers, and none gives anything beyond a name and phone: 211's Weber-Morgan sheet (September 2024) has six Housing / Utilities lines, half of them utilities, and still carries the closed Weber-Davis Habitat chapter; the City's pages cover only its own loans plus the two housing authorities. No list names any rent-help charity, eviction help, affordable (tax-credit) apartments, or Davis County options: OWCAP's family rent help turned up only in a news article, Catholic Community Services' rent help only on an aggregator (needhelppayingbills, unreadable, 403), and Weber Housing Authority's emergency rent help for households outside Ogden City only in a search snippet of a state meeting notice. 211's live search (findhelp) could not be read. Both voucher waiting lists need a call: Ogden's closed in May 2026. Affordable apartments and non-government rent help are where Scout's search still has to do the work.
gaps.id-recovery: Thin. No Ogden or Weber County list has an ID or documents section: the 211 Weber-Morgan Resource List (Sept 2024) has none, Ogden City's guide is from 2019 and has none, and the Weber-Morgan Health sheet lists only its own Vital Records line. 211 Utah's statewide ID and ID-fee taxonomy pages show only The Road Home in Salt Lake (non-operational/archived); the only Ogden fee-help listing is Lantern House, for its own guests. The best list is the state's verifying-agency list (July 2025), but it names verifiers, not ID providers, and gives no contacts. No Ogden nonprofit that pays for ID was found; the real resources are the government offices (DLD, Vital Records, SSA) plus the state homeless fee waiver. ssa.gov blocked reading, so SSA details come from 211.
gaps.immigration: Thin for Ogden. No official Weber County or Ogden City list of immigration providers exists; the only current list with a Weber section is the state DHHS maternal-health guide (August 2026), and it names just three Ogden providers, one of them a general civil clinic. 211 Utah's Weber-Morgan sheets have no immigration heading, only phone numbers under 'Ethnic / Minority Groups', and the 2024-2025 sheet dropped the Welcome Center for Immigrants; 211's own search returned nothing. Most statewide lists are Salt Lake County providers that fail reach. Refugee resettlement in Ogden is undocumented on any list (news reports only about 15 families). Day-and-time details for the NOMAS Ogden clinic and the Welcome Center's own page could not be found, so Scout would still have to confirm those.
gaps.legal: Thin. No Ogden or Weber County list is dedicated to legal help. The current official lists (Weber-Morgan Health, May 2025) name just two legal resources, Utah Legal Services' Ogden office and the courts' Self-Help Center; 211 Utah's newest Weber-Morgan list (Sept 2024) dropped its legal section entirely, and only its stale 2021-22 list had one. The courts' clinic list shows a single Ogden clinic (Timpanogos at YCC) that the provider's own site does not confirm, nothing in Davis County, and still mentions masks, so it looks partly un-updated since COVID. Everything else is statewide by phone or based in Salt Lake City; immigration legal help for Ogden residents and a current Ogden pro se / bar clinic were not found on any list, so Scout's own search would have to do that work.
gaps.medical-dental-vision: Medical is covered well by one current official list (Weber-Morgan Health Department flyer, April 2026), which names the real front doors: Seager (free), Midtown and its Hope and Children's clinics (sliding fee), WSU dental hygiene and Medicaid. Everything else is thinner or stale: 211 Utah's Weber-Morgan list is names and phones only, has misaligned phone numbers and still lists the Primary Care Network that ended in 2019; 211's own search returns nothing for 'dental' near Ogden; the free-clinic aggregator pads its list with ordinary Intermountain practices; the state rural-health dental guide is a 404 and the AUCH health-centre map a 404. Dental beyond Seager, Midtown and student cleanings is thin (no sliding-fee private dentists, no dental school, no denture help named), and vision for adults rests on Seager alone, with EyeCare4Kids for children only. No list named a free or low-cost pharmacy, hearing help or senior dental (Senior Charity Care Foundation appears only in other regions' senior guides). Seager's address changed in November 2025, which the May 2025 list missed: a reminder these lists drift within months.
gaps.mental-health: Lists exist but are short and overlapping: Weber Human Services is on all five, and beyond it, Family Counseling Service and Clinical Consultants, each list has only 1-6 genuine mental health entries, often mixed with addiction, domestic violence and medical clinics. Only the health department sheet (May 2025) is clearly current; Ogden City's page and both school lists are undated, the WSU list has an old address and a duplicated phone, and the 211 PDF gives phones without addresses. 211's live search did not render to a page read, though its DHHS provider directory (utahdhhs.211utah.org) was readable and useful for checking. Gaps a missionary would notice: almost nothing on free or very low-cost ongoing therapy besides Weber Human Services and Family Counseling Service, no Spanish-language provider confirmed in Ogden, no confirmed phone for the 24/7 McKay-Dee Access Center, and nothing on peer support or clubhouse programmes beyond NAMI.
gaps.reentry-support: Thin. The only Ogden list that is truly about reentry is the Weber County Sheriff's Reentry Success Services page (current, July 2026), and it names partners without contact details; the hands-on front door it describes, the Tuesday Reentry Fair, has no phone of its own. None of the four general Weber lists (211 Utah Weber-Morgan 2024-2025 and 2021-2022, Ogden City Resource Guide, Intermountain Ogden list) has a reentry section. 211 Utah's readable directory pages show no Weber reentry provider beyond the correctional centre, and one of its two reentry listings is archived with a dead website. Aggregators are statewide and Salt Lake-heavy, and one gives NUCCC's fax as its phone. What passes is the county programme plus statewide record-clearing (BCI, Clean Slate Utah); local non-profit reentry help (mentoring, felon-friendly housing, jobs) would have to come from Scout's own search or from calling the Reentry Fair.
gaps.seniors: Thin outside Weber Human Services. 211's own Weber-Morgan lists give seniors only four or five lines (one of them AARP), and the 2022 list is stale. Nearly every real senior resource in Weber County is a programme of the one Area Agency on Aging, so its website was the best list. Senior centres changed in 2025 (county funding cut from five to four; Riverdale now city-run), so older lists are wrong on that. Small centres (Ogden Valley, Farr West, Marriott-Slaterville) have no web page of their own that I found. No list covered in-home care providers, senior housing or senior utility help, which Scout would still have to search for.
gaps.transportation: Very thin. 211's current Weber-Morgan list has no transportation section at all, and the 2022 list names only UTA. The only local list of transport providers is UTA's own Coordinated Mobility page, which covers disability and 60+ programmes, and two of its four Weber entries turned out not to be transport services. 211's DHHS search could not be filtered to transport near Ogden. Nothing found covers Medicaid non-emergency medical rides (the Utah Medicaid pages returned 404 or 403), veterans' rides to the VA, gas or car-repair help, or low-cost car programmes; Scout would have to search for all of those.
gaps.utilities-phone-internet: Thin. The only current local list (211 Weber-Morgan 2024-2025) names just HEAT under Housing / Utilities and nothing for phone or internet. The 2022 list's one local charity programme (Cottages of Hope utility help) is now non-operational, and the aggregator's Ogden charities (St. Anne's, Catholic Community Services, Salvation Army, OWCAP) are stale or not mainly utility help. No list names a current low-cost internet programme for Ogden: ACP ended in 2024, and company plans such as Comcast Internet Essentials appear on no list, so Scout's own search would have to find them. Ogden City publishes no standing water-bill assistance programme; its only one was a 2025-26 shutdown deferral. DWS's HEAT pages returned server errors, so statewide HEAT details were read second-hand from Commerce and 211.
gaps.veterans: Thin. No local, human-maintained veterans list exists for Ogden: Weber County's page is a short set of links, 211's Weber-Morgan list (Sept 2024) has only two veteran entries, and 211 Utah's online search returned nothing readable. The state's Northern Utah VSO page is the real front door but gives phones, not an office. The only Ogden-specific directory is an aggregator (Warriors Fund) whose Vet Center and VA clinic addresses are out of date and whose county-VSO entry is gone. The state's 2026 benefit book PDF returned 404. Small local groups (VFW, DAV, American Legion posts) and any local veteran emergency-money or legal help would need Scout's own search.
